title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. A license plate camera system flagged a stolen Camaro, and deputies acted on that flag against a different car of similar appearance. The gap is at the point of confirmation: the deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car in front of them, so the one piece of evidence that would have connected the alert to the vehicle was never obtained. The stop proceeded anyway, with guns drawn and handcuffs applied, and the error was recognised only after the men were restrained.

The failure mode is a system used outside the conditions it was built for. A plate camera identifies a vehicle by its plate, and the stop was made without a plate match. What would have caught it is a positive plate reading before force was used, which is a step available to the deputies on the scene and to the helicopter overhead. The alert was treated as sufficient on its own, and the physical check that the system's output depended on was skipped.

What is not established is any finding of wrongdoing. The sheriff's office said supervisors will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed, and that review had not produced a conclusion in the reporting. Both men plan to file internal affairs complaints, and Anthony's mother said she plans to hire an attorney. A planned complaint is not a filed one, and a planned attorney is not a lawsuit.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies surrounded a Camaro driven by Anthony, 19, as he left with Julian, also 19. Deputies thought the car was stolen, pointed guns, handcuffed both men, and a helicopter circled while at least five patrol cars arrived. The sheriff's office said license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a similar car, but deputies and the helicopter could not read its plates, so they called backup. After the men were handcuffed, deputies realized it was the wrong car.

The men were not charged and were given information about filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, which both plan to do. Anthony's mother said she plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body worn camera video to check whether proper procedures were followed.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
